The flaw can let an attacker corrupt memory and potentially run code.   PHP says  the flaw can be reached through the cURL extension when the extension decompresses HTTP responses automatically. cURL leaves that off by default, but applications and HTTP client libraries can turn it on. web.title: Two Critical Wasmtime Flaws Could Let Malicious WebAssembly Modules Escape Sandboxes
web.description: Two critical flaws in  Wasmtime , a WebAssembly runtime that can be built into other software, could allow a malicious WebAssembly module to escape the sandbox intended to contain it, the project's maintainers say.   An attacker would first need a vulnerable Wasmtime build to compile a module they control, and one of the flaws affects only ARM64 systems. Fixed versions were released on October 19 and 20, and the maintainers have not reported any attacks.   Wasmtime runs WebAssembly code outside web browsers. Both bugs are in Cranelift, the compiler it uses by default to turn WebAssembly into machine code. Wasmtime's maintainers at the Bytecode Alliance rated each flaw 9.9 out of 10 on the CVSS scale in advisories published on October 19. web.title: Between alerts: What Attackers Do in the Spaces Ordinary Detection Misses
web.description: Every SOC struggles with a pile of alerts. Very few of those alerts explain how an attack started or how it progressed. Network data, like that from a network detection and response (NDR) platform, connects individual alerts into one timeline, and it feeds the defensive systems that can tie all events together into one coordinated view.   SOC teams often first see the shape of an intrusion through a series of smaller alerts that are triggered (e.g., when a signature matches a known malware hash, a threshold flags an unusual spike in failed logins, or an endpoint agent detects suspicious activity). web.title: uCreator Android Spyware Can Steal Telegram 2FA Passwords and Clone WeChat Accounts
web.description: A rentable Android spyware kit called uCreator  takes over Telegram and WeChat accounts by hiding its code inside working copies of the two apps, researcher Ovi found . It only reaches people who install one of these tampered copies, spread outside the official app stores, or who run WeChat inside the kit makers' own container app.   The kit's Telegram part matches Baohuo , a backdoor that Doctor Web reported in October 2025 . The Hacker News compared the two reports. web.title: Gheist Uses Stolen GitHub Tokens to Steal Private Repository Secrets via Actions Logs
web.description: An automated campaign is using stolen GitHub tokens to plant workflows that print a repository's secrets into its GitHub Actions logs, which the attackers then download before deleting the runs. The attacks have succeeded in private repositories and GitHub Enterprise environments, according to an analysis by cloud security company Wiz.   A  GitHub safeguard  that pauses suspicious workflow runs stopped every public-repository run Wiz checked, but it does not cover private repositories or GitHub Enterprise Server.   Each workflow sits on a new branch named ci-sync- followed by six random characters. Deleting a branch, or the run it started, does not undo the exposure. web.title: Malicious File in Downloads Folder Tries to Trick AI Coding Agent Into Installing Malware
web.description: A malicious instruction file sitting in a developer's Downloads folder tried to make their AI coding agent install a known-malicious npm package, security firm Forever Security said in a report published last week.   The company caught the attempt on a real customer's machine and stopped the agent before any code ran. It could not determine how the file got into the folder.   The file was  AGENTS.md, a plain-text instructions file that a coding agent, such as OpenAI's Codex, reads when it starts in a folder and follows as directions.   It was dressed up as ordinary engineering notes. One section told the agent to add a server to its own configuration and install a package called function-color from npm.
